note:
2100 -> 2019 (-81). One JSDoc token in web/core/utils/patch.js: the extension parameter is `U & ThisType<T & U>` instead of `U`.

An object literal types its own `this`, so inside every `patch(X.prototype, {...})` in the
codebase `this` was the LITERAL, not the patched class. Reads of the base class through it
were errors and reads of the patch's own additions were errors, and the annotation looked
complete the whole time. `ThisType<T & U>` names both halves: the target and what this patch
adds to it. The `Partial<T>` constraint is deliberately kept -- dropping it costs the
contextual typing of overridden methods' parameters, measured at +391 implicit-any errors in
web/static/tests alone, which is worse than what it buys.

Only files carrying `// @ts-check` are checked under the base config, and in practice that is
web, so the whole move lands in web/static/tests:

    100 errors gone, 19 new, net -81

The 100 are TS2339 x83 (this.<base member>), TS2353 x14, TS2740 x2, TS2345 x1. The 19 new are
the SAME condition reported more precisely, not a regression: a test patch that adds a member
the target does not declare used to surface as one TS2345 against `Partial<T>` at the call
site, and now surfaces as a TS2353 naming the property. clickbot.test.js x7 and
command_service.test.js x2 are that shape.

Measured on a detached worktree at 32166d5bc28 with the workspace node_modules symlinked, both
arms back to back: HEAD 2100 (exactly this floor), HEAD+change 2019. The other two typecheck
gates move the same way and neither verdict regresses -- scope_gate strict and noimplicitany
report the identical REGRESSED sets as HEAD, with four exception entries newly CLEAN and
delisted here, and no excepted-file budget rises.
